scorecards.inningsCommentary: South Africa commenced their first innings at Mangaung Oval, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 143 from AK Markram, complemented by a commanding 247-run stand between Francois Plessis and HM Amla that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 4.74 RPO. Bangladesh's bowling response was spearheaded by Subashis Roy (3/117), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Finishing at 573/4 (119.6 ov), South Africa established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Mangaung Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as South Africa posted 573/4 (119.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Bangladesh countered with 147/10 (42.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 5-Wicket Spell: Kagiso Rabada (5/30), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Kagiso Rabada delivered a masterclass for South Africa (10 Wickets), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (South Africa 81%) and allowing South Africa to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. South Africa's bowling unit, bolstered by AK Markram (143 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing South Africa won by innings & 254 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: South Africa's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, South Africa won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
